closing.reason: HOLDS. Resolution of #1263 is sound: the issue's requested exemption is unsafe and no rule the catalog supports separates its reader from one that cannot see the copies. (a) Soundness, checked in pgpm_prv-15: tests/333 under mutant snapshot_wait_foreign_floor_exempt (a session exempt when another database runs a xid at least as old as its xmin and the reference) passes LIVENESS 1-7 (B and I agree on datid, backend_xmin = X's xid, backend_xid null, type, state, wait event; both began after the last copy) and fails 16: I's read of t333a misses all 19 rows (26..494), keeping only 2600, i.e. #1241's empty read; also fails 8-11 (swapped). Exact-equality to the foreign xid would pass I too (its xmin is exactly X); snapshot import is recorded nowhere a caller reads, and the exporter E has committed by swap time, so any history rule would need new state recorded at the copy's commit, which the copying transaction cannot observe. Waiting matches CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. (b) Entry points: _snapshot_wait has two callers, _regrain_snapshot_wait (regrain_step by hand and maintain ticks) and pgpm_hypertable from_hypertable_cutover (install.sql:1816), both through the changed function; pgpm_archive and uninstall.sql have no copy of the mechanism. regrain() and an unrecorded regrain_written_xid (upgrade path) use the own-xid reference, where every open snapshot is waited for and no holder is named, as documented and pinned by tests/333 part C. (c) Body promises: holder found across databases (pg_stat_activity.backend_xid, visible to every role) and pg_prepared_xacts; a snapshot's xmin is set by running xids only, so no xid-less session, slot or standby feedback can hold the floor unnamed. Residue tried and not claimed: once X ends while B's READ COMMITTED statement keeps running, B stays listed (xmin still X) and the refusal falls back to the generic message with no holder to name; head docs/reference.md documents that drop-out ('the sessions it held back drop out as they release theirs (a READ COMMITTED one when its statement finishes)'), it is bounded by the local statement, and B is again indistinguishable from I-type snapshots whose holder has also ended. (d) Mutations: snapshot_wait_holder_this_database_only alone restores THIS defect (the holder looked for in this database only, so the refusal names innocent local pid B with no holder); snapshot_wait_foreign_floor_exempt restores the issue's requested (unsound) behaviour, not the defect, and serves as the guard that the wait is kept. (e) Contract change: the refusal is the same one the base gave, now documented and legible; no documented workflow newly refused.
